paragraphs.source_en: My thoughts turned sharply back to the present. I heard the outgoing CO come to the end of his speech. I stood, and with the words “I relieve you,” became the commanding officer of *Santa Fe*. I turned to Commodore Kenny and reported I had relieved as CO *Santa Fe*.

I heard the outgoing CO come to the end of his speech.
I stood, and with the words “I relieve you,” became the commanding officer of *Santa Fe*.
I turned to Commodore Kenny and reported I had relieved as CO *Santa Fe*.

paragraphs.source_en: I was ready to go to work. We were scheduled to deploy in 172 days. As I looked across at the officers, chiefs, and sailors assembled on the pier, I knew we should start in the middle. We would start with the chiefs.

paragraphs.source_en: Going to sea in a submarine, leaving your family for six months, is hard work. Honorable work, but hard work. These guys weren’t going to become rich looting enemy ships; they weren’t in it for themselves. Fear was pervasive and we needed to turn that around.

paragraphs.source_en: Connecting our day-to-day activities to something larger was a strong motivator for the crew. The connection was there but it had been lost. Instead, in ways large and small, I encountered situations where the crew’s actions were motivated by following a checklist, pleasing an inspector, looking good, or some other variant of “avoiding problems.”

The connection was there but it had been lost.

Instead, in ways large and small, I encountered situations where the crew’s actions were motivated by following a checklist, pleasing an inspector, looking good, or some other variant of “avoiding problems.”

paragraphs.source_en: I, we, needed everyone to see the ultimate purpose for the submarine and remember that it was a noble purpose. I also wanted to connect our current endeavors with the submarine force’s rich legacy of service to and sacrifice for the country. Once the crewmen remembered what we were doing and why, they would do anything to support the mission. This was a stark contrast to earlier, when people were coming to work simply with the hope of not screwing up.
